correctness.rationale: The proof identifies the eight-neighbour convolution in the correct 5k by 5ℓ periodic quotient, splits the quotient into 25 local factors, checks the nine zero eigenvalue factors, and constructs explicit complete cyclic bases. Eight nontrivial zeros have a simple u-adic leading term giving L chains of length K each; the trivial zero has a quadratic leading term giving 2L chains of length K/2, with the base K=1 handled separately. Fitting decomposition gives all exact transient counts and sharp T=K. Independent direct GF(2) matrix rank calculations test all predicted ranks on nine sample sizes, including a 1600-dimensional case. Computations are corroborating, not substituted for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text primary comparisons show the same eight-neighbour multiplier was known, and a general multivariate periodic quotient framework was known in 1984. The claim is narrower and computationally nontrivial: exact nine fifth-root zero modes, separate K and K/2 Jordan ladders, and all-state transient counts on the full 5-times-dyadic rectangular family. These formulas and a dominating exact result were not located. Novelty remains bounded by accessible sources and search coverage.
residual_risks: Some historical works may be unindexed or inaccessible; absence of a matched title is not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The eight-neighbour Moore XOR rule is a historically studied natural cellular automaton, and its finite periodic attractor structure is an independent dynamical invariant not accessible from a single-seed growth count. The fifth-root resonance gives exactly nine singular frequencies and the characteristic-two doubling creates two distinct nilpotent Jordan scales (K and K/2), yielding sharp, unbounded convergence depth, recurrent-state codimension and exact last-step proportions for every torus in a natural arithmetic family. This is an infinite-family structural classification, not an arbitrary finite table or routine numerical gain.
